rationale: Response A is better because it gives a cleaner driver-based framework, highlights the crucial nonlinear effect of rising CAC as online channels saturate, and clearly distinguishes digital traffic acquisition from location-driven foot traffic and physical throughput constraints. Its comparison is structured, actionable, and appropriately recommends bottom-up forecasting, scenarios, and forecast-error tracking. Response B adds useful points on inventory, returns, and omnichannel attribution, but makes several overly broad or questionable claims, including near-zero online marginal cost, systematically lower in-store transaction values, and hard shelf-capacity limits, while overstating how readily rich data makes standard time-series methods effective.
